core.title: State an own metric on a plan artifact whose dimension+direction pair is deliberately unmapped
core.given: A plan artifact carries a dimension with an upward direction (maximize or increase) — a dimension+direction pair the dimension→metric mapping table deliberately marks unmapped.
core.when: You create or edit that plan artifact.
core.then: The plan artifact states its own metric instead of inheriting a table default.
prefer: Treat the plan artifact as legal: an unmapped pair is a deliberate omission, not an error.
Remember the direction synonyms: both spellings of the upward intent are unmapped exactly alike.
avoid: Inheriting a default — including reusing the dimension's downward metric for the upward intent.
core.why: No upward metric was ever chosen for the deliberately unmapped dimensions; their only defaults are downward, so there is nothing valid to inherit.
evidence: Reviewer confirms the plan artifact states its own metric and does not rely on a table default; this rule prescribes neither where the metric is stated nor a threshold.
verification: Advisory at source severity 2: findings of this rule are reported for review, not enforced (source-level disposition advisory).

Review-enforced, not check-enforced: the automated metric-mapping check selects only plan artifacts whose pair maps to a default metric id; plan artifacts on unmapped pairs fall outside its selector, so the obligation is verified by review.

Unmapped pairs are exactly those the stack's dimension→metric mapping table marks with its unmapped sentinel, each carrying a stated reason it has no default; the concrete set of unmapped pairs, the sentinel's spelling and the per-pair reasons are data of that table, deferred to the realization.
The unmapped mark plus a stated reason lets a reader tell a deliberate omission from a missing table row.

Rationale the check may assume: every unmapped dimension names only a downward default, and the table's other dimensions pair each intent with a different metric, so an upward default cannot be the downward metric reused — it would have to be a metric never chosen.

fires: A planner authors a plan artifact carrying a dimension+direction pair the mapping table deliberately leaves unmapped
A planner edits such a plan artifact, whichever synonym spelling of the upward direction it uses
doesNotFire: A plan artifact on any pair the mapping table maps to a default metric — the companion executable-bar rule's subject
A downward direction (minimize/decrease) on those dimensions — the table maps it to a default metric
Editing only the mapping table or the plan-artifact schema's enums — the companion table-totality rule's subject

neutralityNotes: The subject was neutralized to the plan-artifact role (local kind 'desired outcome' and path 'plan/**' via profile keys roles.plan_artifact.kinds / roles.plan_artifact.path). The dimension→metric mapping table is convention-family data, not stack structure, so no profile key is proposed for it: the core refers to it generically and — like roots.excluded deference — defers the concrete unmapped set ({effort, frequency}×{maximize, increase}), the `unmapped` sentinel spelling, the per-pair reasons and the table name dimension_metric to the realization (bunOnly). Dimension and direction names (effort, frequency, maximize, increase) and metric ids are treated as the ATDD criteria vocabulary shared across stacks; only their concrete occurrences as examples stay in bun.json, the delivered reference. Companion Bun rule ids (.desired-outcome-executable-bar, .table-totality) were generalized to 'the companion executable-bar / table-totality rule' in doesNotFire. Source-level severity 2 / advisory disposition and the validator selector scope are carried in core.verification, not as profile keys.
